name: Ghamoo-ra
summary: In Blackfathom Deeps, Ghamoo-ra guards a small island in the Pool of Ask'ar. The ancient giant turtle tramples anyone who comes near.

sections.title: A Beast of the Drowned Temple
sections.body: Blackfathom Deeps was once a night elven temple to Elune. Flooded now, the ruins are claimed by naga, satyr, and the nihilistic Twilight's Hammer cult. Ghamoo-ra dwells among them, his enormous, thick shell turning aside all but the most determined blows.

sections.title: Guardian of the Deeps
sections.body: Lesser turtles surround Ghamoo-ra on a small island in the Pool of Ask'ar, and they leave travelers be. He alone attacks, crushing anyone who comes near beneath his trampling bulk.

faq.answer: Ghamoo-ra guards a small island in the Pool of Ask'ar within Blackfathom Deeps, the flooded temple of Elune held by the Twilight's Hammer. He attacks anyone who approaches.

faq.q: Why is Ghamoo-ra hostile to outsiders?
faq.answer: Nothing is recorded of how Ghamoo-ra came to be so savage. He attacks anyone who intrudes on his island in the Pool of Ask'ar, trampling all who come near.
Yes. Despite his size and years of torment, a skilled hunter can tame Ghamoo-ra.

faq.q: What is the Pool of Ask'ar?
faq.answer: The Pool of Ask'ar is a flooded subterranean cavern in Blackfathom Deeps. Ghamoo-ra roams the center of a small island there, surrounded by docile native turtles.

faq.q: What connection does he have to the Old Gods?
faq.answer: None is recorded. Ghamoo-ra is a beast of the deep, while Twilight's Hammer cultists who worship the Old Gods have overrun the sunken temple around him.

angles.text: As a hunter venturing into Blackfathom Deeps, you may pity Ghamoo-ra, a noble, ancient beast of the deep. With patience, you may yet tame him.
As a night elf, you may see Ghamoo-ra's savage presence in Elune's drowned temple as a bitter reminder of how far the sacred site has fallen to the vile Twilight's Hammer.
As a druid, you find in Ghamoo-ra an ancient creature of the deep, grown savage amid the ruins of the defiled temple.
